body:
Perhaps `is_constructible()` isn't quite the right name. Built-in types are constructible, just without `.new()`. Since this method is only intended for objects, an error should be printed for unexpected types.

```suggestion
			ERR_FAIL_V_MSG(false, "GDScript bug: Unexpected datatype kind.");
```

> Perhaps `is_constructible()` isn't quite the right name. Built-in types are constructible, just without `.new()`.

Maybe `is_constructible_object()` would be the most accurate, then?

> Since this method is only intended for objects, an error should be printed for unexpected types.

Hmm, this would probably print an internal error if i.e. `int.new()` is used with the current implementation, then. Should the checks against built-in and enum types be added back there?

Also, the tests for scripts and inner classes (added in this PR) seem to fail even though the implementation looks correct (`is_constructible()` returns `false` for them). Is there any other points for them in this call stack that could suggest `new()`?

> Is there any other points for them in this call stack that could suggest `new()`?

The `new()` method is likely found from a base class that is not abstract (in this case `RefCounted`).

Alright, I hope I fixed it (by adding the recursion restriction to finding base classes here as well). It didn't seem to fail any other tests, so I think it's safe.

I also adjusted the switch cases so that your suggestion would work perfectly, and renamed it to `is_constructible_object`.

```suggestion
```

Built-in and enum types are also unexpected in a method intended for objects.

+    {"display": "new(…)"},

body:
```suggestion
exclude=[
    {"display": "new(…)"},
    {"display": "new()"},
    {"display": "new"},
]
```

This does exact comparison. A change to the display format should not invalidate the test cases.
Please move this into editor code for the time being. We can move it if we need it in the analyzer, but until then I don't think it belongs here.

```suggestion
			ERR_FAIL_V_MSG(false, "GDScript bug (please report): Unexpected datatype kind.");
```

Also could we move the check to the start of the function. Having contracts easily readable at the start of the function is IMO good practice.

Should it still be a function (for clarity's sake) or should it be directly in the function it's used in `_find_identifiers_in_base`? I imagine there might be a few other editor cases in the future, but not sure.
To be clear, do you mean move `default` up, or make it `ERR_FAIL_COND_V_MSG`? The latter would make the check more complex, I'm sure.
Huh, it turns out the check that was there originally (in `master`) was unnecessary, too. It can be removed entirely I guess.

Judging by your comment about abstract native classes above, "Whether a type can be constructed must be checked based on the most specific type." would _technically_ be false (since the check still occurs in `is_constructible_object`). But eh, I can't think of anything else atm that would be more accurate to it. Maybe "Only check if the most specific type is constructible at recursion depth 0"?
Keeping it a function sounds good to me.

I did mean `ERR_FAIL_COND_V_MSG` but I was under the assumption that we had an easy way to check for object types. But given that I can't seem to find that, my memory is probably playing a trick on me. Feel free to disregard that part.
I think "most specific" is fine. The instance base type of a script is kind of a property of that specific script type.

```suggestion
			return p_datatype.class_type && !p_datatype.class_type->is_abstract && !ClassDB::is_abstract(p_datatype.native_type);
```

Or is there a particular reason you used `p_datatype.class_type->base_type.native_type`? (Like in theory this should be the same, but our initialization for `DataType` is a bit over the place, so I'm unsure if you are working around some specific issue.)
You removed `base_type.kind != GDScriptParser::DataType::BUILTIN`. Why? I'd assume there is some edge case, why it is there.

I removed it before I added the error, and even after testing, it didn't error like enums did. Maybe because it doesn't count as a metatype, so that's why the condition is never `true` even without the specific check. Idk if that might change later on though, so I'll add it.

I tried it and the test failed for some reason (I didn't test why). Maybe the native type isn't set for it, so it's returning `&""`, probably. But for the class type's base type, it is. I think it'll be fine if this is used for now.

In that case we need to add an `is_empty` check before calling to `ClassDB`. New ClassDB code usually prints an error if the name is not a valid class. And we want stay silent for autocompletion.

(Edit: Like we need to check that even if it usually works with `base_type`, if it can fail for one of them there could be edge cases were it would be empty for base_type as well)
